The image contains two line plots, labeled (a) and (b), which illustrate the performance of various language models during training. The x-axis in both plots is labeled "Training Steps" and spans from 0 to 140,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss w.r.t. FLOPs" and is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from $10^{-1}$ to $10^{1}$, with major tick marks at $10^{-1}$, $10^{0}$, and $10^{1}$.

Plot (a) shows the loss with respect to FLOPs for different methods. The "Vanilla" method (solid black line) starts at a loss of approximately $10^1$ and steadily decreases. The "StrmLLM" method (dashed red line) starts at a loss of approximately $10^1$ and decreases to a loss of approximately $10^{-1}$ at 140,000 steps. The "SepLLM" method (dashed blue line) starts at a loss of approximately $10^1$ and decreases to a loss of approximately $10^{-1}$ at 140,000 steps.

Plot (b) shows the loss ratio with respect to FLOPs for different methods. The "Vanilla" method (solid black line) starts at a loss ratio of approximately 1 and decreases to a loss ratio of approximately $10^{-1}$ at 140,000 steps. The "StrmLLM" method (dashed red line) starts at a loss ratio of approximately 1 and decreases to a loss ratio of approximately $10^{-1}$ at 140,000 steps. The "SepLLM" method (dashed blue line) starts at a loss ratio of approximately 1 and decreases to a loss ratio of approximately $10^{-1}$ at 140,000 steps.
